summary: ph-common ships install- and import-time beacon to hardcoded bare-IP endpoint
details: The package is a hollow stub: `main` exports a Proxy returning no-op functions for any property access, so it provides none of the functionality its generic name implies. Its only real behavior is `beacon.cjs`, which POSTs the installer's hostname, install path, cwd, and Node version to the hardcoded bare-IP HTTP endpoint http://185.158.107.175:8787/_ah/dc. The beacon is wired to run both as `scripts.postinstall` (fires on `npm install`) and from the top-level of `index.js` (fires on `require()`), so any installer or build system that resolves this package automatically discloses host identifiers to the operator of that IP. The stub-plus-beacon shape, the generic namespace-friendly name (`ph-common`), the anonymous bare-IP + plain-HTTP destination, and the cover-story comment claiming only 'provenance' are consistent with a dependency-confusion / namesquat reconnaissance payload against internal build systems.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
